scope.b0Requirement: Freeze the design, inputs, scoring and reproducible baseline; no optimization candidate is required for B0.
scope.applicationRequirement: A fixed candidate must pass a fresh admitted confirmation cohort before production application.
scope.population: Independently authored benchmark source families admitted under this protocol; not the population of real user conversations.

sampling.withinFamily: Average all predeclared eligible outcomes over all three repetitions in each version, then subtract control from candidate.
sampling.betweenFamilies: Equal family weights; questions, repetitions and worker turns are not independent samples.
sampling.allocation: Draw each family independently from the frozen eight-stratum mixture with probability 1/8 per stratum; record the schedule before authoring sources and before any model run. Metric eligibility depends on the authored scenario, never on outputs. Register N separately for each metric. A per-stratum claim requires its own adequate eligible cohort; eight-stratum coverage alone is not subgroup power.
admission: Distinct underlying source graph, actors, chronology, dependencies and constraints; replacing names or numbers alone does not establish independence.
All derived questions, revisions, paraphrases and source lineage remain in one family and one split.
Audit template dependence; merge correlated sources into a larger cluster and count that cluster once.
Gold and prohibited outcomes are derived from sources, checked before model execution and kept out of model inputs.
Use synthetic or separately authorized sources; do not read private conversations to create samples by default.
Freeze the cohort manifest and hashes before either version is run; retire the cohort from unseen confirmation once any outputs are inspected.
sampling.order: Seeded random AB/BA order within each family and repetition; record the seed and complete schedule.
sampling.failures: Timeouts, parsing failures and rejected requests remain in the denominator and consume recorded resources; a missing outcome cannot be replaced by a successful rerun.

inference.reference: Maurer and Pontil (2009), Theorem 4, scaled from [0,1] to [-1,1], union bound for both tails
inference.halfWidth: sqrt(2 * unbiasedSampleVariance * log(4 / alpha) / n) + 14 * log(4 / alpha) / (3 * (n - 1))
inference.confirmationIndex: j starts at 1 and increases for every revealed formal candidate comparison across both stages; never reset it after failures or between stages.
inference.allRequiredMetrics: Every declared criterion must pass. This is an intersection-union decision; individual intervals do not claim simultaneous coverage.
inference.bootstrapRole: Existing family bootstrap intervals remain descriptive; they do not replace the decision interval or increase the independent sample count.

qualityRoute.ceilingRule: If a +5pp absolute improvement is unattainable, this quality route cannot authorize application. Do not switch to relative error reduction after viewing candidate outputs; a separate design must be frozen before such an experiment.

efficiencyRoute.positiveImprovementInterval: Predeclare a valid upper bound B for every logical request, including retries. For each family use (meanControlCost - meanCandidateCost) / B in [-1,1]; its empirical Bernstein interval lower bound must be >0. The relative point estimate is 1 - meanCandidateCost / meanControlCost, with positive control cost.
efficiencyRoute.outOfRangeCost: Do not clip, drop or rescale after observing results; an exceeded registered bound or unknown usage makes this comparison insufficient for application.

samplePlanning.method: Normal approximation for planning only, using the registered empirical Bernstein width evaluated at the hypothesized paired variance; not an achieved-power guarantee.
samplePlanning.varianceModel: D in {-1,0,1}; P(D=1)=(q+delta)/2, P(D=-1)=(q-delta)/2, Var(D)=q-delta^2. Three repetitions are conservatively treated as fully correlated for planning.
samplePlanning.registeredN: Use the larger of the route minimum, the planning calculation for its next confirmation index, and every required outcome/stratum sample requirement. For efficiency also size the cost primary using a separately registered bounded-cost effect and variance from independent exploratory data. Families not eligible for a metric do not count toward its N. Multiples of eight are a batching convention, not fixed stratified allocation.
samplePlanning.atThresholdWarning: A true +5pp benefit has at most about 50% probability of satisfying a >=5pp point-estimate gate under a symmetric continuous approximation, even with unlimited N; +8pp is the planning alternative, not a lower application threshold.
samplePlanning.assumptionFailure: If independent preconfirmation pilot evidence does not support the registered variance/effect assumptions, freeze a larger N before revealing any confirmation output. An underpowered completed comparison is insufficient evidence, not a failed optimization for the stopping rule.

protectedOutcomes.subgroups: Report every registered important group. An observed decline beyond its predeclared tolerance, a critical failure, or unmeasured required resources prevents application; do not hide groups in an overall average.
protectedOutcomes.costAccounting: Count all attempts and retries per logical request; preserve failures, unknown usage and timeouts. Report p50, p95, mean, calls, input/output tokens, startup, event-loop delay, peak memory, index size and update cost where applicable.
protectedOutcomes.p95Method: Compute the empirical p95 over the fixed registered logical-request mixture. Keep each family and its repetitions intact in descriptive resampling; do not claim a rigorous p95 confidence guarantee from the mean interval.

preregistration.beforeRunning: Freeze and hash this registration before either version sees the confirmation sources.
preregistration.results: Retain complete single-step and cumulative-versus-stage-baseline results, including failures and all original outputs.
preregistration.analysisRepair: A scorer or fixture defect invalidates the affected comparison; retain the reason and rerun both versions. An exposed cohort becomes regression data, so a claim of unseen confirmation requires a fresh admitted cohort.
preregistration.stopping: No interim significance checks or outcome-driven sample extensions. Infrastructure failure, incomplete data and insufficient power do not count as one of the three measured unsuccessful candidate experiments required to stop a stage.
preregistration.sequence: Finish and apply a confirmed retrieval improvement, freeze and remeasure B2, then begin task-context optimization. A protocol or baseline completion is not an optimization application.
